description: Real lowRISC/CHERIoT-fork Ibex (ibex_top) at the pinned revision, composed as the instruction+data OBI master pair of the generated SoC. Endpoints, clocks, resets and every remaining top-level port come from the official interface description and from the RTL itself; the four aggregate ram_cfg_icache_* ports are declared unrepresentable (see evidence.unknown) and are therefore out of the bounded elaboration.

resets.release: rst_ni is the single active-low asynchronously asserted reset of ibex_top (rtl/ibex_top.sv:318,632,642); deassertion must satisfy clk_i recovery/removal timing, and the core only leaves reset into fetch once fetch_enable_i holds ibex_pkg::IbexMuBiOn.

capabilities.evidence: Widths come from the elaborated facts: instr_addr_o/data_addr_o/instr_rdata_i/data_rdata_i/data_wdata_o are 32 bits, data_be_o is 4 bits (= data_width/8, which the OBI plugin's extension policy checks against wdata), and both master endpoints carry an error response, so byte_enable/error_response describe the data and read-only instruction OBI interfaces respectively. max_outstanding is declared 1 because that is the OBI capability limit and the single-outstanding contract of obi_processor_memory_adapter that this phase composes; ibex_top itself permits up to two outstanding data accesses for a single unaligned load or store (rtl/ibex_top.sv:228-236, MaxOutstandingDSideAccesses=2), which the generated single-outstanding fabric deliberately does not admit. This is a composition limit, not a claim about the core's full concurrency.

port_actions.reason: DFT / clock-gating test enable: ibex_top wires it into prim_clock_gating u_core_clock_gate_i (rtl/ibex_top.sv:332-337). Holding it at 0 keeps the gated core clock in functional mode; src/myfuzz/composition/rtl/soc_ibex_beat_core.sv ties the same port to 1'b0.
rtl/ibex_cs_registers.sv:430 returns it as CSR_MHARTID. This SoC composes exactly one hart, so the single-hart identity 0 is the only correct value; soc_ibex_beat_core.sv drives 32'd0.

Reset-vector base. rtl/ibex_if_stage.sv:243 sets PC_BOOT = {boot_addr_i[31:8], 8'h80} and rtl/ibex_if_stage.sv:199 records boot_addr_i[7:0] as unused, so 0x10000 makes the first fetch 0x10080, inside the request's rom0 window 0x10000..0x18000. 0x10000 is this profile's declared cpu.reset_vector and the value configs/soc/ibex-pulp.json uses for the same core.

CHERIoT TRVK revocation-bitmap heap base. The parameters keep BaseIsa at its default BaseIsaRV32I, so ibex_top generates gen_no_cheriot_trvk and sinks this input (rtl/ibex_top.sv:1320-1349); 0 is the disabled value and matches soc_ibex_beat_core.sv (32'd0).

Instruction-read integrity sideband. SecureIbex=0 makes MemECC 0, so ibex_top generates gen_non_mem_rdata_ecc and sinks instr_rdata_intg_i (rtl/ibex_top.sv:362-367). The OBI instruction path composed here carries no ECC bits, so 0 is the declared inactive value.

Data-read integrity sideband, sunk through trvk_rdata_intg by gen_non_mem_rdata_ecc (rtl/ibex_top.sv:362-367) because MemECC is 0 with SecureIbex=0; the OBI data path carries no ECC bits, so 0 is the declared inactive value.
CHERIoT data-tag sideband; gen_no_cheriot_trvk folds it into unused_trvk (rtl/ibex_top.sv:1328-1346) because BaseIsa is RV32I. 0 is the disabled value (soc_ibex_beat_core.sv drives 1'b0).

CHERIoT revocation-bitmap response. gen_no_cheriot_trvk sinks it and drives trvk_revbm_req_o and trvk_revbm_addr_o to '0 (rtl/ibex_top.sv:1322-1346), so the channel is inactive and 0 is the declared idle value.
CHERIoT revocation-bitmap response valid, sunk by gen_no_cheriot_trvk (rtl/ibex_top.sv:1328-1346); the channel is inactive, so 0 is the declared idle value.
CHERIoT revocation-bitmap read data, sunk by gen_no_cheriot_trvk (rtl/ibex_top.sv:1328-1346); no request is ever issued, so 0 is the declared idle value.
CHERIoT revocation-bitmap read-data integrity, sunk by gen_no_cheriot_trvk (rtl/ibex_top.sv:1328-1346); no request is ever issued, so 0 is the declared idle value.
CHERIoT revocation-bitmap error response, sunk by gen_no_cheriot_trvk (rtl/ibex_top.sv:1328-1346); no request is ever issued, so 0 (no error) is the declared idle value.

Machine software interrupt. The composition's interrupt plan routes exactly one machine-external level source into irq_external_i, this profile's declared entry; the SoC has no CLINT/software-interrupt source, so the input is held inactive (Ibex machine interrupts are active-high levels). soc_ibex_beat_core.sv ties it to 1'b0 as well.
Machine timer interrupt. No timer source is composed (the interrupt plan declares only the machine-external entry), so the input is held inactive; soc_ibex_beat_core.sv ties it to 1'b0 as well.

15 local (fast) interrupt bits. No local interrupt source is composed and the interrupt plan only drives the machine-external entry, so every fast bit is held inactive; soc_ibex_beat_core.sv drives 15'd0 as well.
Non-maskable interrupt. The SoC composes no NMI source and the interrupt plan declares none, so the input is held inactive rather than left floating; soc_ibex_beat_core.sv drives 1'b0.
ICache scramble key valid. ICacheScramble keeps its default 1'b0, so ibex_top generates gen_noscramble and sinks this input (rtl/ibex_top.sv:657-671); no key is present, so 0 is the disabled value.
ICache scramble key, sunk by gen_noscramble (rtl/ibex_top.sv:657-671) because ICacheScramble is 0; all-zero is the declared disabled value.
ICache scramble nonce, sunk by gen_noscramble (rtl/ibex_top.sv:657-671) because ICacheScramble is 0; all-zero is the declared disabled value.

Debug entry request. This profile declares no debug endpoint (a debug transport would need a debug_slave protocol contract that this composition request does not provide), so debug entry is held disabled: ibex_core enters debug mode on a high level and ibex_top keeps the core clock alive for a pending debug request (rtl/ibex_top.sv:322-331). soc_ibex_beat_core.sv drives 1'b0 as well.

ibex_pkg::IbexMuBiOff is 4'b1010 = 10 (rtl/ibex_pkg.sv:760). The parameters keep BaseIsa at its default BaseIsaRV32I, so the CHERIoT base ISA is not selected and the MuBi 'off' pattern is the declared disabled value (soc_ibex_beat_core.sv drives ibex_pkg::IbexMuBiOff).

ibex_pkg::IbexMuBiOn is 4'b0101 = 5 (rtl/ibex_pkg.sv:759). rtl/ibex_core.sv:648-649 gates instruction fetch on fetch_enable_i == IbexMuBiOn, so the core must be enabled for the whole test; soc_ibex_beat_core.sv drives ibex_pkg::IbexMuBiOn.

rtl/ibex_cs_registers.sv:845 makes CSR_MCOUNTEREN writable only when mcounteren_writable_i == IbexMuBiOn (= 4'b0101 = 5, rtl/ibex_pkg.sv:759); soc_ibex_beat_core.sv drives IbexMuBiOn and this profile declares no separate control for it.

DFT scan reset, active low. SecureIbex=0 means the lockstep block is not generated, so ibex_top takes gen_no_lockstep and sinks the input (rtl/ibex_top.sv:1262-1263). Holding it deasserted (1) is the functional-mode value; soc_ibex_beat_core.sv drives it from reset release.

Security alert output (minored, rtl/ibex_top.sv:1355-1359). It is a component output with no in-SoC consumer: nothing in the fabric, the adapters or the interrupt controller samples it, so the generated SoC exports it for passive monitoring only.
Major internal security alert (rtl/ibex_top.sv:1355-1360); status output with no in-SoC consumer, exported for passive monitoring only.
Major bus security alert (rtl/ibex_top.sv:1355-1360); status output with no in-SoC consumer, exported for passive monitoring only.
Clock-gating status, assigned ~clock_en (rtl/ibex_top.sv:331). Output, so it can only be observed: exported for passive monitoring only.

Crash dump of the trapped instruction (current_pc/next_pc/last_data_addr/exception_pc/exception_addr, ibex_top.sv:132 and 471). Status output; it stays one flat observation entry covering all five members and is exported for passive monitoring only.
Sticky double-fault status from ibex_core (rtl/ibex_top.sv:471). Status output, exported for passive monitoring only.

Data-write integrity sideband. SecureIbex=0 makes MemECC 0, so ibex_top generates gen_no_mem_ecc and drives it to constant 0 (rtl/ibex_top.sv:862-869). It is an output, so it cannot be tied off by the SoC; it is exported for passive monitoring only.
CHERIoT data-tag output, driven to constant 0 by gen_no_cheriot_trvk (rtl/ibex_top.sv:1322-1327) because BaseIsa is RV32I. Output, exported for passive monitoring only.
CHERIoT revocation-bitmap request, driven to constant 0 by gen_no_cheriot_trvk (rtl/ibex_top.sv:1322-1327). Output, exported for passive monitoring only.
CHERIoT revocation-bitmap request address, driven to constant 0 by gen_no_cheriot_trvk (rtl/ibex_top.sv:1322-1327). Output, exported for passive monitoring only.
ICache scramble key request, driven to constant 0 by gen_noscramble (rtl/ibex_top.sv:666) because ICacheScramble is 0. Output, exported for passive monitoring only.
Lockstep compare enable. With SecureIbex=0 ibex_top generates gen_no_lockstep and drives it to IbexMuBiOff (rtl/ibex_top.sv:1255). Output, exported for passive monitoring only.

Shadow-core data request of the redundant lockstep core, driven to constant 0 by gen_no_lockstep (rtl/ibex_top.sv:1256-1261) because Lockstep=SecureIbex=0. Output, exported for passive monitoring only.
Shadow-core data write enable, constant 0 under gen_no_lockstep (rtl/ibex_top.sv:1256-1261). Output, exported for passive monitoring only.
Shadow-core data byte enables, constant 0 under gen_no_lockstep (rtl/ibex_top.sv:1256-1261). Output, exported for passive monitoring only.
Shadow-core data address, constant 0 under gen_no_lockstep (rtl/ibex_top.sv:1256-1261). Output, exported for passive monitoring only.
Shadow-core data write data, constant 0 under gen_no_lockstep (rtl/ibex_top.sv:1256-1261). Output, exported for passive monitoring only.
Shadow-core data write integrity, constant 0 under gen_no_lockstep (rtl/ibex_top.sv:1256-1261). Output, exported for passive monitoring only.
Shadow-core instruction request, constant 0 under gen_no_lockstep (rtl/ibex_top.sv:1256-1261). Output, exported for passive monitoring only.
Shadow-core instruction address, constant 0 under gen_no_lockstep (rtl/ibex_top.sv:1256-1261). Output, exported for passive monitoring only.

semantics: configs/cpus/ibex/official_core_interface_description.json (endpoint ids, functions, protocols, role-to-port aliases, pinned file list and elaboration parameters)
src/myfuzz/protocols/plugins/obi.json and src/myfuzz/composition/processor_adapters.py (OBI role directions, widths and the read-only instruction adapter)
configs/soc/ibex-pulp.json (top parameters and reset_vector for the same core)
src/myfuzz/composition/rtl/soc_ibex_beat_core.sv (the project's own wiring of ibex_top, used as a cross-check for every constant and for the disabled-feature inputs)
verified: Physical ports, directions and widths come from verilator-json elaboration of the pinned closure with ICache=0, PMPEnable=0, RV32E=0, SecureIbex=0 - the parameter set configs/soc/ibex-pulp.json uses for this core.
Every constant is grounded in the RTL line that consumes or sinks the port, and matches the value the project's own wrapper drives for the same parameterization.
Every observe entry is an output that the same RTL drives (to a status value or to a constant in this parameterization); no component output is driven by the SoC.
unknown: The four top-level aggregate ports ram_cfg_icache_tag_i/ram_cfg_icache_tag_o/ram_cfg_icache_data_i/ram_cfg_icache_data_o (packed arrays of prim_ram_1p_pkg::ram_1p_cfg_req_t / ram_1p_cfg_rsp_t, two ways of a 12-bit request and a 1-bit response) cannot be represented by the current verilator-json port extractor: source_elaboration.py rejects a top-level aggregate without member paths. source.top_port_selection="declared" therefore elaborates only the ports this profile binds, and these four ports are NOT elaborated, NOT classified and NOT connected in the generated SoC. With ICache=0 ibex_top takes gen_norams and drives the two response ports to prim_ram_1p_pkg::RAM_1P_CFG_RSP_DEFAULT while sinking the two request ports (rtl/ibex_top.sv:844-849), so no reachable behaviour is lost in this configuration - but the omission is a real coverage gap of the frontend and is recorded here instead of being hidden.
The SoC does not verify that ibex_top boots or executes: the profile and this phase prove composition structure and port disposition only.

Capability values (address_width/data_width/max_outstanding/byte_enable/error_response) are declared from the elaborated widths and the OBI adapter contract; no runtime transaction of this composed SoC was executed here.
